problem: Given that ${i,j}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,4⟩$ and $⟨5,-1⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation in Terms of the Standard Basis

feedback.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$
